title: trace-compare-facet-workflows-brainstorm
content:
Purpose and context:
- Quick exploratory doc capturing different interaction models for comparing traces, expressing trace filters as a small facet-driven language, and lightweight wireframe sketches for the console. Not a final spec; meant for grooming with SRE and UI engineering.

Background/problem:
- Users frequently need to understand differences between two or more requests: why one had a 120ms tail latency vs another 40ms, or why tokens spiked for a particular route. Current trace viewer shows a single waterfall; comparing across traces requires mental mapping and repeated toggling.
- Goal: make 'compare' a first-class operation with minimal context switch, preserve span alignment, and enable ad-hoc filtering/aggregation via a compact facet language.

High-level success criteria:
- Reduce time-to-insight for trace comparison by 40% (measured in user task tests).
- Allow engineers to create and persist filter facets for common debugging queries.
- Keep UI performant when showing 2-4 traces side-by-side or an aggregated timeline.

User stories / examples:
1) As an SRE I want to pin two traces (A and B) and see aligned span timelines so I can spot which stage added the extra latency.
2) As a backend engineer I want to apply a facet filter "db.duration>50ms" and have matching spans highlighted across selected traces.
3) As a platform engineer I want to open a comparison between a sample of 10 traces and a baseline average to detect regressions in span counts.
4) As a PM I want to save a compare-view as a named investigation and attach notes for later review.

Interaction model options (sketches + tradeoffs):
A) Side-by-side synchronized waterfalls (primary candidate)
  - Layout: vertical split, N columns (default 2), each column shows standard waterfall with spans, metadata header, and ability to expand/collapse spans.
  - Synchronization: vertical alignment by trace timeline using percent or absolute timestamps. Hover on span in any column highlights matching spans (by operation name) in other columns and draws a light connector line.
  - Pros: Familiar, direct comparison, easy to inspect span internals.
  - Cons: Screen real estate heavy; may be cramped for deep traces.

B) Unified stacked timeline with per-trace lanes
  - Layout: single waterfall where each trace is a lane; lanes are stacked vertically with a shared time axis.
  - Sync: spans align to the global time axis. Option to normalize start times to zero for relative comparison.
  - Pros: Easier to scan timing differences across many traces, compact.
  - Cons: Harder to see nested spans relationships when lane widths are small.

C) Diff overlay mode (dense)
  - Layout: baseline trace drawn in light gray; compared trace overlays in color, with delta markers and annotations for spans that diverge (duration delta>threshold).
  - Pros: Highlights deltas directly.
  - Cons: Visual clutter for many differences; accessibility concerns.

Quick ASCII wireframe (Side-by-side candidate):
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Header: trace compare — [Traces: 2] [Save view] [Export CSV] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
| Left pane (controls)  | Column A (Trace A) | Column B (Trace B) |
| - Search / facets      | Header: trace id, route | Header: trace id, route |
| - Saved queries        | Waterfall (spans)      | Waterfall (spans)      |
| - Time alignment toggle| Span inspector panel (collapsible) for selected span  |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
Notes on interactions:
- Pinning: right-click on any trace in the main listing -> Pin to compare. Allow multi-select checkboxes and `Compare` button.
- Drag-to-reorder columns.
- Hover connectors: small bezier lines drawn between matched operations; there should be a toggle to disable connectors for performance.
- Keyboard flow: 'c' to open compare modal, arrow keys to move focus between lanes, 'p' to pin a span.

Facet language design (compact, human-readable):
- Intention: keep filters accessible to non-SREs while expressive enough for typical queries. Use a small DSL with field comparisons and logical ops.
- Examples: 
  - route = "/v1/generate" and db.duration > 50ms
  - span.op contains "kv.get"
  - status != OK
  - token_count >= 1024
- UI: provide a chips-based input where each facet can be created via autocomplete (field operator value), and a text-mode toggle shows the equivalent DSL string. Saved facets are reusable.

Highlighting and matching heuristics:
- Primary matching key: span.operation (op name).
- Secondary heuristics: span.tags.service, span.tags.db.statement fingerprint, and approximate duration bucket (fast/normal/slow).
- Allow manual mapping: user may mark span X in trace A as 'equivalent to' span Y in trace B to force connectors if automatic matching fails. Record mapping as a one-off annotation for the compare session.

Performance considerations:
- Lazy-render spans outside viewport; virtualization per column.
- Limit default compare to 2 traces; allow up to 4 with a warning and automatic summarization.
- Provide aggregated mode: compute per-operation mean/std and show small sparkline instead of full waterfall when many traces selected.

Backlog grooming (tasks, rough estimates, owners):
- UX: Finalize wireframes for side-by-side and stacked timeline (3d) — Rina (3d)
- Infra: API endpoints for bulk trace fetch + pre-aligned timeline payload (5d) — Jasper (5d)
- Backend: facet query engine extension (support range queries and duration units) — Tom (4d)
- Frontend: compare modal, column layout, connectors (8d) — EngConsoleTeam (8d)
- QA: Perf tests, accessibility checks (3d) — QA Team (3d)
- Docs: short how-to + save-view UX doc (1d) — Product Docs (1d)

Open questions / discussion items:
- Matching strategy: should we prefer span.operation equality or hash of (operation, service, parent.op)? Tradeoffs: strict matches miss renamed operations; fuzzy matches risk false positives.
- Saved compare views: should they capture raw trace ids or query that regenerates traces? Storing queries is more resilient.
- Export format: CSV with per-span diffs vs a JSON bundle.
- Access controls for compare: should compare sessions respect the same access controls as individual traces? (Probably yes)

Next steps before grooming meeting:
- Rina to produce high-fidelity mock for side-by-side and stacked lanes (due 2025-01-20).
- Jasper to prototype an API payload shape for aligned timelines and share example on the linked PR.
- Tom to draft a short proposal for facet DSL syntax with parsing examples.
- Sync: 2025-01-23 10:00am PT — invite SRE, frontend, and a sample customer success rep for feedback.

Notes / scratch ideas (quick wins):
- Add a small comparator badge in the trace list rows so users can quickly select and add to compare basket.
- Use color-blind friendly palettes and earned marks for delta coloring.
- Desktop first; revisit mobile view after we validate core flows.

Attachments and references:
- See linked JIRA and PR for initial backend hooks.
- Related: existing trace viewer heatmap widget (product/console-and-rollouts) — may reuse sparklines.

End of doc.
